intro: The UVC/UAC Depth Calculator estimates insertion depth for umbilical venous and umbilical arterial catheters from birth weight, using the Shukla/Dunn formulas plus an adjustment for umbilical stump length. It reports separate depth estimates and target anatomical positions for the UVC (venous) and UAC (arterial, with weight-banded low/high-line options), alongside bedside best-practice guidance on catheter positioning and dwell time. The tool is built for neonatal clinicians placing or checking umbilical lines and is explicitly intended for use alongside X-ray confirmation.
indications: Estimating UVC insertion depth before placement in a neonate requiring central venous access
Estimating UAC insertion depth for arterial access or monitoring in a sick neonate
Cross-checking catheter depth against birth weight and umbilical stump length at the bedside
Anticipating expected tip position (e.g. T8–T9 for UVC) before reading a confirmatory X-ray
Reviewing best-practice timing for catheter replacement or removal to reduce infection or thrombosis risk
method: UVC depth (cm) = (3 × birth weight in kg + 9) / 2, plus umbilical stump length; target tip position T8–T9, 0.5–1.0 cm above the right diaphragm. UAC depth (cm): for birth weight ≥ 1500 g, (3 × BW kg) + 9, plus stump length; for birth weight < 1500 g, (4 × BW kg) + 7, plus stump length; target position is Low (L3–L4) or High (T6–T9). The source file also references two research add-on methods not exposed as separate inputs: the Wright birth-length method (UVC = 0.5 × shoulder–umbilicus length + 1) and a Dunn surface-length method using crown–heel length.

faqs.q: What formula does the app use for UVC depth?
faqs.a: (3 × birth weight in kg + 9) / 2, plus the umbilical stump length, targeting a tip position at T8–T9.

faqs.q: Does the UAC formula change with birth weight?
faqs.a: Yes — the app uses (3 × BW kg) + 9 for babies ≥ 1500 g and (4 × BW kg) + 7 for babies < 1500 g, both plus stump length.

faqs.q: Why does umbilical stump length matter in this calculation?
faqs.a: The calculator adds the stump length to the calculated depth because the underlying formulas are referenced from the abdominal wall, not the cut end of the cord.

faqs.q: Is a high or low UAC line preferred?
faqs.a: The app's best-practice notes state a high UAC (T6–T9) carries lower thrombosis/vascular compromise risk than a low UAC (L3–L4) and is preferred where practicable.

faqs.q: How is catheter position confirmed after placement?
faqs.a: The app specifies confirming both lines on an AP chest/abdominal X-ray before infusing inotropes or hyperosmolar fluid.
